title: Decision: OPER answers 491 and CONNECT, SQUIT, KILL, WALLOPS answer 481
description:
The verbs OPER, CONNECT, SQUIT, KILL and WALLOPS cannot apply to a
single-user agent with no server link behind it. Bead mimid-1wgh.140.2
replaces their 421 with the numeric each verb's own reply list gives.
Four readings had to be settled to write those two match arms.

WALLOPS: 481, NOT THE 421 ITS SECTION MANDATES. WALLOPS is the only one
of the five under Modern's "Optional Messages"
(~/PROJECT/IETF/specs/ircdocs-modern.html, h2 id="optional-messages" at
:2829), whose preamble at :2832 is one sentence with two halves: "These
messages are not required for a server implementation to work, but
SHOULD be implemented. If a command is not implemented, it MUST return
the ERR_UNKNOWNCOMMAND (421) numeric." That MUST is the document's only
occurrence, so the tension exists for WALLOPS alone.

  Reading A: mimid does not implement WALLOPS, so 421 is mandatory.
  Reading B: the MUST is about a command the server does not have, and
  ERR_UNKNOWNCOMMAND's own definition (:4146) says what it means --
  "Sent to a registered client to indicate that the command they sent
  isn't known by the server." A verb the server parses, recognises and
  refuses is outside that definition, and WALLOPS's own reply list
  (:2955) offers ERR_NOPRIVILEGES (481) for the case where the sender
  may not send one (:2946, "Servers may generate it themselves, and MAY
  allow operators to send them").

CHOSEN: B. 421 under Reading A and 481 under Reading B describe
different facts, and 481 is the true one: mimid knows the verb.
WALLOPS's SHOULD is declined, as AGENTS.md requires a declined SHOULD to
be cited and explained: Modern :2939 makes WALLOPS a message "to all
currently connected users who have set the 'w' user mode for
themselves", and an agent has one user, whose own notices already arrive
through the service nick.

OPER: 491 ERR_NOOPERHOST, NOT 464 ERR_PASSWDMISMATCH. OPER's reply list
(ircdocs-modern.html:1321-1334) offers 461, 464, 491 and 381. 464 is for
a wrong password (:1311) and 491 for a server "not configured to allow
connections from this client's host to become an operator" (:4359).
mimid's case is the second: no operator block exists at all. 464 is also
unavailable on its own terms, because it presupposes a comparison
against a configured password, and comparing a credential in the
registered-command dispatch would be a second authorization boundary --
AGENTS.md puts the one IRC boundary at the credential checked before
registration ends (mimid-agent-irc/src/register.rs). 381 RPL_YOUREOPER
and the MODE message Modern :1317 pairs with it are never sent.

~/PROJECT/meshIRCd, the epic's second reference, diverges here: its
handleOPER (main.go:2630-2632) answers 464 when operPass is empty, and
reads msg.Params[1] to do it. That divergence is the argument for 491:
the oracle's answer costs a password comparison mimid will not make.

THE REFUSAL COMES BEFORE ANY PARAMETER COUNT. `OPER` alone, `WALLOPS`
alone and `KILL` alone answer 491 or 481, never 461. Modern fixes no
order: 461 is in all five reply lists, OPER's text says "Both parameters
are required for the command to be successful" (:1311), and
ERR_NEEDMOREPARAMS (:4236) is defined as the answer when a command
"cannot be parsed because not enough parameters were supplied".
meshIRCd goes both ways -- handleKILL refuses a non-operator before
counting (main.go:2643-2655), handleOPER counts first (:2624-2628).

CHOSEN: refuse first, for all five. It is the only arrangement in which
no parameter of OPER is read, so a user who mistypes their local token
into `OPER alice <token>` never has it in a variable, let alone in a
comparison or a log. The cost is that a client cannot learn the verb's
arity from mimid, which no client needs for a verb mimid will never
honour.

723 ERR_NOPRIVS IS NOT USED, though CONNECT (:1973), KILL (:2733),
SQUIT (:2818) and WALLOPS (:2958) list it beside 481. Its shape is
"<client> <priv> :Insufficient oper privileges." (:4479): it presupposes
an operator who lacks one named privilege, and the <priv> name would
have to be invented. The user here is not an operator, which is what 481
says.

THE TEXTS ARE PINNED THOUGH THE SPEC LETS THEM VARY. 421 (:4146), 481
(:4332) and 491 (:4359) each say "The text used in the last param of
this message may vary". mimid sends Modern's literal strings --
"Permission Denied- You're not an IRC operator" with no space before the
hyphen and an ASCII apostrophe, and "No O-lines for your host" -- and
the integration test pins the bytes, so a reworded string is caught. The
wording is mimid's choice, not a conformance requirement; meshIRCd's
handleKILL (main.go:2649) sends the same 481 string.

Numbers come from ~/PROJECT/IETF/specs/ircdocs-modern-numerics.yml:
ERR_NOPRIVILEGES '481' at :635, ERR_NOOPERHOST '491' at :647,
ERR_UNKNOWNCOMMAND '421' at :500, RPL_YOUREOPER '381' at :404.
close_reason: Settled from Modern and the code during mimid-1wgh.140.2; the five arms carry the pointer.
